before.question: What's the practical difference between SIGTERM and SIGKILL?

options.correct: SIGTERM (15) can be caught or ignored by the process and allows graceful shutdown; SIGKILL (9) is forced by the kernel and cannot be caught, blocked, or handled

options.distractor_2: SIGTERM only works on background processes; SIGKILL is required for foreground processes and shell builtins
options.distractor_3: SIGTERM is the legacy signal name; SIGKILL is its modern replacement and both have identical behaviour in current Linux kernels

SIGKILL is the no-questions-asked tool of last resort. Distractor 1 reverses the two. Distractor 2 invents a foreground/background distinction. Distractor 3 (modern replacement) is fiction — both signals have been stable since early Unix. Production apps should handle SIGTERM properly so SIGKILL is never needed.
